summary:
SPHEREx Sky Explorer – Discover the Universe, One Movement at a Time

The universe is constantly changing, but discovering those changes hidden in billions of astronomical observations is a major challenge. To make this exploration easier, we developed **SPHEREx Sky Explorer**, an interactive web-based platform designed to bring the power of NASA's SPHEREx mission closer to everyone.

Our platform allows users to explore specific regions of the sky using Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) coordinates, visualize astronomical observations, and compare images captured at different times. Its spectral image viewer and observation dashboard help users explore infrared data and understand changes in celestial objects through a simple, user-friendly interface.

By transforming complex astronomical information into an accessible visual experience, our solution aims to support the identification of moving objects, variable stars, and potential new discoveries. It bridges the gap between advanced space science and public participation, encouraging students, astronomy enthusiasts, and citizen scientists to explore the universe.

**Our vision is simple: Make the universe easier to explore, one image, one observation, and one discovery at a time.**
details:
SPHEREx Sky Explorer – Turning Billions of Stars into Opportunities for Discovery

What if discovering a new object in the universe was as simple as comparing two pictures?

The universe is constantly moving and changing, but identifying these changes across billions of astronomical observations is a challenge. Our team developed SPHEREx Sky Explorer, an interactive web platform inspired by NASA's SPHEREx mission, to make exploring these cosmic changes simpler, smarter, and accessible to everyone.

How Our Project Works:

Instead of making users navigate complicated astronomical datasets, our platform provides a simple starting point: sky coordinates. Users enter Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec) to explore a selected region of the sky. The platform includes coordinate validation, an observation results dashboard, and a spectral image viewer to make astronomical information easier to investigate and understand.

What Makes It Valuable:

Our idea focuses on turning complex astronomical observations into a visual discovery experience. By supporting the exploration and comparison of observations from different times, the platform aims to help users investigate moving celestial objects, variable stars, brown dwarfs, and other interesting phenomena.

Technology Behind the Innovation:

We developed the platform using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, with Visual Studio Code as our development environment, GitHub Copilot for AI-assisted development, and GitHub for version control and project hosting.

Creativity, Accessibility and Future Impact:

Our innovation lies in bringing coordinate-based exploration, observation monitoring, and spectral visualization together in one beginner-friendly platform. We considered usability, accessibility, performance, visual clarity, scalability, and future integration of real SPHEREx datasets and other astronomical resources.

Our vision goes beyond displaying images. We want to make astronomical exploration an opportunity for everyone, where students, enthusiasts, and citizen scientists can take part in understanding our changing universe.

Because the next great astronomical discovery might not begin in a laboratory. It might begin with someone curious enough to compare two images of the sky.
